episodes.title: Is AI Racing Toward Disaster? — With Tristan Harris
episodes.description: Tristan Harris is the co-founder of the Center for Humane Technology. He joins Big Technology to discuss AI risk, what the leading labs understand about their models, and whether the industry needs to slow down. Tune in to hear why Harris believes AI’s growing ability to deceive evaluators and evade oversight should change how we approach its development. We also cover China’s AI progress, the motivations of researchers pursuing superintelligence, and whether governments can coordinate to prevent dangerous outcomes. Hit play for a probing conversation about AI’s benefits, its risks, and what it would take to keep humans in control. Learn more about your ad choices. Visit megaphone.fm/adchoices

episodes.title: Replay: On Food as Medicine (2020)
episodes.description: What if one of healthcare’s most powerful interventions isn’t a drug, but food? Originally recorded in 2020, this conversation looks at how nutrition could help prevent and manage chronic disease while lowering healthcare costs. Julie Yoo speaks with Dr. Andrea Feinberg and Plated co-founder Josh Hix about food insecurity, medically tailored meals, reimbursement, and why access and convenience can matter as much as knowing what’s healthy. They also discuss how online grocery shopping and delivery could reshape people’s food environments, and what it would take to make nutritious food a more integrated part of healthcare. episodes.title: Wikipedia: Jimmy Wales. The Man Who Trusted Strangers to Build an Encyclopedia (2018)
episodes.description: While running an internet search business in the late 1990s, Jimmy Wales began exploring an ambitious idea: an encyclopedia built for the web. His first attempt relied on experts and moved painfully slowly. But in 2001, he launched Wikipedia, inviting volunteers to write, edit, and fact-check articles on virtually any subject. What began as a radical experiment grew into one of the world's largest reference resources, built by volunteers and freely accessible to anyone with an internet connection. episodes.title: Marc Levinson on How UPS Created Modern Logistics
episodes.description: UPS was founded nearly a century ago in the basement of a Seattle saloon by James E. Casey and his business partner Claude Ryan. They initially called the company American Messenger Company, and the first iteration of the firm that became UPS was a bike courier service. It is now hard to imagine modern, globalized life, and the logistics required to prop it up, without the innovations Casey and his partners at UPS cooked up during the company's early decades. Marc Levinson has just written a biography of Casey and the company he founded — UPS Man: James E. Casey and the Creation of Modern Logistics — which was a lot harder to do than you might imagine, because Casey shunned the spotlight and his contributions were virtually unknown outside of UPS. episodes.title: クレーム解決で課金？企業価値4.7兆円に倍増したシエラの狙いとは
episodes.description: 米AIスタートアップのシエラ（Sierra）が、約2,780億円の新規調達を実施し、企業価値がわずか半年で倍増の約4.7兆円に達しました。従来のトークン数や利用量ベースの課金とは一線を画し、顧客の問い合わせや苦情の解決など、完了したタスクに応じて課金する成果報酬型のビジネスモデルが注目を集めています。フォーチュン50の半数近くをはじめ、大手金融機関など規制の厳しいエンタープライズでの導入が急速に進んでおり、直近の年間経常収益（ARR）は約636億円を突破しました。巨額のAI投資に対する回収懸念が囁かれる中、なぜ同社は圧倒的なスピードで成長を遂げ、投資家から高い評価を受け続けているのか。大企業が求めるカスタマーサービス自動化の最前線と、シエラが示す最新のAIエージェント動向について詳しく解説します。
